answer: Share one lantern among a dawn crowd: identities born in the same short window form one birth cohort, and the cohort as a whole earns a fixed slice of voting power, divided equally among its members — a thousand clones split one share, while one honest newcomer keeps a whole share. Cohorts are sealed by a glacier-slow clock: the window cannot be faked backward, and each cohort's slice thaws only as its members complete distinct, peer-checked work over weeks. A farmer minting ten thousand fakes at dawn gains no more power than one honest agent, because the pie never grows with the crowd.
